title: Guelph to Goderich trail bridge over Conestogo River
subtitle: Fountain Street North and Fischer Hallman expropriations, traffic controls, 2026 road construction, Ion speed and Frederick Street cycling limits.
overview: The Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee recommended a two-span trestle pedestrian bridge over the Conestogo River at Wallenstein for the Guelph to Goderich trail {{vote:m6}}. Staff said the project is estimated at $8.26 million. Community donors and the township cover most of that, and the Region would fund the remainder from the general tax-supported capital reserve. Delegates said many trail users now turn back at the river crossing.

The committee also recommended starting expropriation for the Fountain Street North widening in Cambridge {{vote:m5}} and approved more expropriations for Fischer Hallman Road in Kitchener. It recommended new traffic controls in Kitchener, Cambridge and Woolwich {{vote:m4}}, and added land along Northfield Drive East in Waterloo to the Regional Road System.

Councillors heard a report on 2026 regional road construction. Staff said provincial Bill 60 limits planned cycling lanes on Frederick Street. A delegate from a transit advocacy group spoke on Ion light rail speed, and staff described planned crossing and signal improvements. These recommendations go to Regional Council for final adoption.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended the two-span trestle bridge design, filing the environmental assessment notice, funding agreements with two community donors, and a capital budget amendment.
The committee recommended authorizing the Regional Solicitor to apply to expropriate land and easements for widening Fountain Street North between Kossuth/Fairway Road and Middle Block Road.
The committee recommended approving expropriation of temporary easements for improvements between Bleams Road and Plains Road, running to the end of 2028.
The committee recommended amending Traffic and Parking By-law 16-023 to install new traffic controls in Kitchener, Cambridge and Woolwich.
The committee recommended a by-law adding lands at 300 Northfield Drive East, Waterloo, to Regional Road 22 and registering notice on title.

debate: Councillors supported the bridge but asked about long-term costs: staff said the bridge has a 75-year lifespan, the Region would own it, and it would be added to the Asset Management Plan. Several councillors asked for a clearer financial plan for eventual renewal.

One councillor was concerned about drawing on reserves given the Region's finances and asked whether more fundraising or a different reserve could be used. A delegate said further fundraising would delay construction and risk losing the private donors. Staff said the surplus was recommended for the operating contingency reserve.

Delegates and councillors cited trail use, cycle tourism and safety, noting that many trail users turn back at the Conestogo River crossing. One councillor asked whether the Region could be recognized more in the trail's name; the delegate pointed to signage and map boards.

On Fairway Road, a councillor asked about traffic calming before a new secondary school opens. Staff pointed to lower speed limits, flashing beacons and the roundabout safety pilots, and said they would keep monitoring.

On road construction, a councillor said Bill 60 overrides Council's decision for Frederick Street cycling lanes. Others asked for township projects to be listed separately, and about Cedar Street, Queen's Bush Road and Schneider Road.
